metadata.note: WEEKLY PROGRESS REEL for the loon-detector project, week of 2026-09-04. Eight-beat weekly-progress spine of WEEKLY-VIDEO-GUIDE.md. THE WEEK, as reported by the author, verbatim in scope: (1) annotation is COMPLETE on every image he quality-checked last week; (2) about 136 images are now ready to be trained on the latest YOLO vision model; (3) he supplied one labelled image to include, val_batch0_labels.jpg. THROUGH-LINE: the quality check ran BEFORE the labelling, so the set is small on purpose — nothing was annotated that was going to be thrown away, and a small clean set is the only version still cheap to change. DOUBLE-CHECK LAW — THE ONLY FIGURE THE AUTHOR SUPPLIED IS 'about 136 images'. It is spoken as 'about a hundred and thirty-six' and written '136' only where the author's own qualifier travels with it. NO mAP, accuracy, precision, recall, epoch count, image-size, batch, train/val split ratio, class count beyond the one visible class, or annotation-hours figure appears anywhere — none were supplied. NO YOLO VERSION IS NAMED. The author said 'the latest YOLO vision model' and did not say which release, so every mention on screen and in voice is 'the latest YOLO' and never v8/v11/v12/YOLOv-anything. NO TRAINING RUN IS CLAIMED: he said the set is READY to be trained, so the reel says nothing has been trained yet — consistent with week one. COUNTS ON THE B02 PLATE ('16 tiles', '8 of 16 tiles', 'one class: common loon') are counts of WHAT IS VISIBLE ON THAT PLATE, not dataset totals, and the plate is captioned to say so. The three capture paths (web stills, a Nikon from shore, a drone over open water) are READ OFF the web_/nikon_/dji_ filename prefixes in the supplied mosaic — that is evidence, logged in SOURCES.md, and it is the one inference this reel makes from the image. The 'corcommon loon' string on the drone tile is TWO OVERLAPPING BOX CAPTIONS in the mosaic plot, not a mislabelled instance; nothing in the reel treats it as a data error. ILLUSTRATE LAW: Claude UI at B00, B06 and the verdict/outro only; the four body beats run ChipGrid -> STILL -> DivergentFates -> BinaryBranch, no two consecutive patterns repeated. B04's train-now-or-wait fork is an EDITORIAL ARGUMENT the voice poses, not a decision the author reported — see PEDAGOGY.md. SHORTS / 9:16: every Remotion pattern here has a registered *916 portrait sibling (ClaudeComposerAsk916, ClaudeScienceChipGrid916, DivergentFates916, BinaryBranch916, ClaudeVerdictArtifact916, ClaudeTitleOutro916), so shorts.py rewires the reel with no new TSX. B02 is user media and would otherwise be centre-cut — a centre cut keeps the middle 37.5% of the sheet's width and would slice two columns in half — so it is covered by a hand-composed pantry/B02-916.png built by make_plates.py: eight of the sixteen cells, re-tiled 2x4 and ordered as a largest-to-smallest scale ramp. B02 motion is 'hold', NOT kenburns: compile.py's zoompan pushes ~8% outward and would clip the outer cells, and the range across the whole sheet is the beat. NARRATION CARRIES NO POSITIONAL REFERENCE ('top left', 'two rows down') because the same mp3 plays over both plates and the cell order differs between them. typeScale 1.4 on the two deck patterns, which were authored against a 1280x720 stage; the *916 siblings take {data} only and ignore it harmlessly. Deck-pattern label/detail strings are kept short — fixed-x SVG text does not reflow, so a long label overprints silently and Remotion still exits 0. BRANDING RULE 7: slot-1 kicker stays 'Computational Skepticism'.

beats.narration_text: Last week the boxes were a promise. This week the promise closed. This is Sai. Every image that passed quality control last week is now annotated — about a hundred and thirty-six of them, one class, common loon, every box drawn by hand. That set is ready for the latest YOLO. And a hundred and thirty-six is a small number. It is supposed to be, because each one had to get past a check before it was allowed to count.

In some frames the bird fills half the picture. In others the box is smaller than its own caption — a dark smudge, a few pixels across, on open water. Same label. The same model has to find both.

See make_plates.py.

beats.narration_text: That is not one detection problem. It is two, wearing one name. Close in, the bird is unmistakable — the collar, the beak, the red eye, hundreds of pixels of evidence. Far out, all of that is gone, and what is left sits on water that moves and glints. The near frames will make this model look good early. The far ones are where it actually gets judged.

beats.narration_text: So: train now, or keep annotating? A hundred and thirty-six frames is a small set, and the pull is to wait until it is big enough to win on. But the first run is not a test of the detector. It is a test of the plumbing — that the labels parse, the classes map, the loss moves. Better to know that before there are a thousand more boxes to redo.

props.artifactHeading: Loon detector · week two, one page
artifactLines: Annotation is complete on every image that passed quality control last week — about 136 frames, one class, common loon, with every box drawn by hand.
The order was deliberate. The quality check ran first, and only the images that cleared it were annotated. Nothing was labelled that was going to be thrown out later.

The set spans three capture paths — web stills, a Nikon shot from shore, and drone frames over open water — so subject scale runs from half the frame down to a few dark pixels. One class label covers all of it.
Nothing has been trained yet. The set is ready for the latest YOLO, and while it is still this size it is also still cheap to change.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. If you have a labelled set sitting ready, do not train it yet. Open the label file and sort every box by area. Look at the smallest tenth, then the largest. If those two groups do not look like the same problem, you do not have one dataset — you have two, and one average score is going to hide whichever of them is failing.

the running line settles — one average score hides the half that is failing

props.command: Take a labelled detection set I already have and sort every box by pixel area. Put the smallest tenth beside the largest tenth and show me both. Then tell me whether those two groups are the same detection problem — and if they are not, what a single average score is hiding.

props._contract_note: LogoOutro, NOT ClaudeTitleOutro. ClaudeTitleOutro's handle is hardcoded to @NikBearBrown (OUTRO-LOCK.md) and cannot carry @HumanitariansAI, which is this series' handle; OUTRO-LOCK scopes that card to claude-liam-* slugs and says other channels use their own outro. LogoOutro is it — it takes `handle` and the humanitarians mark already exists. aspectRatio 0.845 = the SVG's 311/368 viewBox. TIMING TRAP: the composition is 120 frames @30fps = 4.0s and fades to opacity 0 over its last 12 frames, while remotion_scenes.py freeze-extends a short render with tpad=stop_mode=clone — which would clone the FADED frame into seconds of black. So this beat's narration is held to 10 words (~3.0s) to fit inside the card, and the 136-frames recap it used to carry was moved into B05's verdict, where a restatement belongs anyway. `./art run` will print "SKIN LINT: the outro is 'LogoOutro' — OUTRO LAW wants ClaudeTitleOutro": that lint is this deliberate deviation, not a defect.
